title: Large Intestine
summary: The large intestine is the final section of the digestive tract - a wide tube that absorbs water and salts from leftover food and packs the rest into solid waste. Explore how it finishes the job of processing what you eat.

compareCandidate.label: Small vs. large intestine
compareCandidate.description: The small intestine is longer and absorbs nutrients. The large intestine is shorter, wider, and absorbs mainly water while packing waste.

plainLanguageExplanation: The large intestine is the last major part of the digestive system. It is wider than the small intestine but much shorter (about 1.5 meters). By the time food reaches it, most nutrients have been absorbed. The large intestine's main job is to absorb water and salts from the leftover mixture, making the waste more solid. Helpful bacteria live here too, helping process some materials and making some vitamins. The solid waste is stored in the last part (the rectum) until it leaves the body. So the large intestine is where the body salvages the last water and packs up what it cannot use.

whyItMatters: The large intestine recovers water, keeps you hydrated, and packs the body's waste. Understanding it explains why you need fiber and water, and what 'good bacteria' in your gut actually do.
tagline: The water saver and waste packer
didYouKnow: About 1.5 liters of water pass into the large intestine each day - and most of it is absorbed back into the body.
